text: Bramwell Logistics runs a lean three-person SOC, and right now, every high-severity Sentinel incident waits for a human to open it, check the flagged user's sign-ins by hand, and decide whether to revoke their session. That manual lookup eats ten to fifteen minutes an incident. This lab builds the script that automates the lookup and enrichment, while still refusing to act without a gate.

The pipeline starts with a polling function that only looks at high and critical severity incidents created or updated since the last run, and a processed-IDs file that remembers which incidents it has already handled. Without that tracking, a loop re-querying the same rolling time window would reprocess, and potentially re-contain, the same finding over and over.

Before any decision gets made, enrich_incident pulls the flagged user's recent sign-ins through Microsoft Graph and checks any unfamiliar source IPs against a threat-intel lookup -- the exact Chapter 4 pattern, now feeding a live pipeline. Everything this function returns is read-only; nothing here can touch the user's account.

The script never jumps straight from enriched data to a real action. propose_containment builds a plain dictionary describing what it wants to do -- which user, what action, why -- so it can be logged, posted to an approval channel, or unit tested before a single credential is touched.

Exactly one function is allowed to change account state, and it refuses to run unattended. dry_run=True is its default, so a careless invocation only logs. And even with dry_run turned off, a missing approved_by value still raises an error -- two independent guardrails stacked on the one dangerous function in the whole pipeline.

Lesson 29 proved this pipeline works end to end against a canned test fixture, enriching a finding and proposing containment without ever touching a live account by default, and without re-processing an incident it has already handled once. Lesson 30 turns to protecting the script itself, adding a real security gate to the CI/CD pipeline that ships it to Bramwell's production SOC environment.
